assumptions: named sequences - N = 200000, K = 25, pool 1..1500 plus 1500 random n <= N plus the candidates, the known failing pairs as seeds, shifts 0..16
atlas (the 45 base sequences of EXP-C08-02) and the 90 quadratic rows of EXP-C08-04 - N = 50000, K = 12, pool 1..800 plus 800 random, shifts 0..12

window filter - occupancy grid of {c(n) : n <= N}, dilated by one cell; it cannot see failures whose product conjugate lies within one cell of the window (fractal boundaries), which is why the known pairs are added as seeds
a failing pair is certified only by an explicit triple
meta.falsification: A certified failure for Fibonacci at s >= 2 (would contradict the Lean theorem CLM-C08-01); a certified failure at a shift listed as associative by EXP-C08-06 (refutes that row); a positive-beta quadratic row whose no-failure set is not upward closed (refutes CLM-C08-04).
meta.hypothesis: H-C08-7: targeted inputs find certified failures at shifts that random and small-input searches passed (as the Skeptic reports for (2,2;1,2) at s = 6 and (3,3;1,5) at s = 10); after the targeted search, no Pisot sequence with a positive conjugate root has a non-monotone shift set (CLM-C08-04) and no non-Pisot sequence has a shift without failure (CLM-C08-02).
meta.methodology: Candidate inputs with extreme conjugates; exact embedding test on all candidate pairs and on the pool pairs whose product conjugate falls outside the occupancy grid of the window; explicit triples for failing pairs; per sequence, the shifts with a certified failure and the shifts without any failure found.
meta.question: Do the associativity thresholds and the shift sets of EXP-C08-02, -04 and -06 survive a search that targets inputs with extreme conjugate coordinates?
meta.title: Extreme-conjugate search: certified non-associativity for the named sequences, the 45-sequence atlas and the 90 quadratic rows
